description: You are a biomedical engineer conducting pre-deployment fault tolerance validation testing for OpenICE at General Hospital. Hospital administration requires documented evidence that the ICU monitoring system can maintain patient safety when a device adapter unexpectedly fails. Your validation test procedure: (1) Create two identical Simulated Multiparameter Monitor device adapters to simulate a redundant dual-monitor setup. (2) Launch the Vital Signs clinical application and confirm both monitoring devices are visible and streaming data simultaneously. (3) Simulate a device adapter failure by stopping or closing one of the running device adapter instances — observe how you would do this and what method is available in the OpenICE interface. (4) While in the Vital Signs application, observe and document the system's response to the device failure — does it detect the lost device? Does monitoring continue with the remaining device? Are there any visual indicators of the failure? (5) Restore full monitoring redundancy by creating a replacement device adapter. (6) Write a device fault tolerance validation report to /home/ga/Desktop/fault_tolerance_report.txt documenting the complete test procedure, the observed system response at each stage, and your assessment of OpenICE's fault tolerance characteristics and suitability for safety-critical ICU deployment. OpenICE Supervisor is already running on the desktop.

metadata.clinical_context: Device fault tolerance validation for ICU deployment
